messages.subject_clean: Conversion from Skyline to MSstats for PRM analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi Giovanni,

I took a look at your dataset, and I have a few questions:
I saw for the "Fragment Ion" column, there are rows with the values of "precursor", "precursor [M+1]" and "precursor [M+2]".  Could those rows be removed?  From my understanding of SRM/PRM, the first MS scan deals with precursor ions, and the second MS scan handles the fragment ions, but we only care about intensity measurements from fragment ion scans (ref <https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/biochemistry-genetics-and-molecular-biology/selected-reaction-monitoring>).
Are you able to find an "MSstats format" report in Skyline which you can export your data?  From what I know, there should be an MSstats format report in Skyline
Thanks,
Tony

On Thursday, February 29, 2024 at 6:13:10 PM UTC-5 Anthony Wu wrote:
> Hi Giovanni,
>
> Thanks for sharing the data to my work email.  I'll take a look later this/next week.  I saw you added an additional question which I'll add to this google group thread:
>
> As a side question, I wanted to ask you what is the process MSstats does to output the protein intensity with DIA data. If I understood correctly, the process is based on the summarization of product ions intensity, without dealing with precursor ions, am I right?
>
> Yes, your intuition is generally correct.
>
> To be more specific on what MSstats does (ref: section 2.2 in page 10 of the MSstats manual <https://msstats.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/MSstats_v3.18.1_manual_2020Feb26-v2.pdf>) - once raw data (e.g. data from Skyline) is converted to MSstats format, the combination of values in the columns peptide sequence, precursor charge, fragment ion, and product charge uniquely determines a feature.  For each protein, MSstats determines the protein's intensity by taking a summarization of the intensities of the protein's features.
>
> Tony

> > Hi,
> >
> > I know MSstats supports conversions of datasets produced from DIA, DDA, and SRM acquisition types, but I'm not too familiar with PRM.  As a first step, could you provide us the sample data and the annotation file so we could reproduce the error?
> >
> > Thanks
> > Tony
> >
> >
> >
> > On Tuesday, February 27, 2024 at 10:23:10 AM UTC-5 gioc...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > Dear MSstats group,
> > >
> > > I am encountering some difficulties in importing PRM data into MSstats. What I am doing is creating the Report 'Transition Result' from Skyline, which has the info on Peptide, Replicate, Precursor, Fragment Ion, Area etc, and importing an annotation file with the usual architecture, then submitting both of them to the 'SkylinetoMSstatsFormat' function, but I get the error:
> > >
> > > 'Error in .checkDDA(input): **Please check precursors information. If your experiment is DIA, please remove the precursors. If your experiment is DDA, please check the precursor information.'
> > >
> > > Since I believe PRM is quantified at the fragment level, do I have to get rid of the precursor column? Or is there another Report from Skyline I need to export (which I could not find)?
> > >
> > > Thank you in advance for your reply and for developing such a useful tool,
> > > Giovanni
> > >

messages.subject_clean: New Plotly graphs in MSstats and MSstatsShiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

We have just released a refresh of the plots in the core MSstats package using the `Plotly` package. These plots can replace any of the standard plots which are built using `ggplot`. The new plots are interactive, allowing users to zoom into certain regions of the graph and hover over data points to get more information.

To use these new plots you must set the `isPlotly` parameter to TRUE in the `dataProcessPlots` and `groupComparisonPlots` functions. Otherwise the functions will work largely the same as they did before. Example code for creating a profile plot can be seen below:

```
dataProcessPlots(summarized, type="ProfilePlot", featureName="NA",
                                 which.Protein="P00959", address=FALSE, isPlotly=TRUE)
```

All plots in MSstatsShiny are automatically replaced with the Plotly plots in the newest version and there is no option to go back to ggplot.

Finally, we plan on adding this option to the remaining MSstats packages (MSstatsTMT, MSstatsPTM, and MSstatsLiP in that order). Expect this in the coming months.

Feel free to reach out with any questions.

Devon

Tony

messages.subject_clean: Question on DF calculation for GroupComparison with technical replicates
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Thanks for developing this great tool. I have a question on how MSstats uses technical replicates in

My experimental setup is as follows:
Two conditions (mutant, WT) with two and three subjects respectively. Each subject has 3 technical replicates for 15 MS runs in total.

For differential testing, I treated this as a simple group comparison. Different subjects in each condition are distinguished in BioReplicate column (eg. WT.1,  Mut.1, WT.2, Mut.2 etc...).

When looking at the output, I was surprised to see the degrees of freedom were higher than expected (histogram attached). I'd like to have more of an understanding of how DF is calculated in this case; are the technical replicates treated as independent observations?

Thank you,
Martin

messages.subject: MSstatsPTM progenesis questions
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am someone rather
new to (phospho)proteomics analysis and have recently been handed a dataset at
my new job where they asked me to assist with the analysis of a mouse dataset. I
managed the proteomics portion fine (the MSstats guide is really good!) but I’m
struggling with the PTM part and was hoping I could get some feedback
here.

For the PTM part they did
a peptide-level phospho-enrichment, measuring in DDA mode. Then they did a
progenesis aligment and mascot search.

I now have ther progenesis-style output, but there are several elements where I’m not sure if they
could be a problem (the MSstatsPTM guide that I found did not have much info
regarding expected Progenesis input):

1) I have an extra
column that is mostly empty, but which sometimes has 1 (or more) ‘alternative’
Accessions. Is this a problem? Currently I just filter this out.

2) Some rows do not
have a PTM. Should I filter these out? What about when there are multiple PTMs?

3) Most Accessions are
of the format sp| UniProtID|geneID_MOUSE. However, sometimes I also find things
labeled eg. Biognosys|iRT (synthetic peptides for LC-MS standardization?), REV_sp (decoy
protein hits?), tr|A8KBU6|A8KBU6_CON-DANRE (Danio Rerio proteins??) and sp|P05783|K1C18_CON-HUMAN
(proteins incorrectly labeled as human?). What do I do with these, also just
throw them all out?

4) In addition to
these questions, after I run ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat I find that I cannot
run dataSummarizationPTM due to “Missing columns in the PTM input:
PeptideSequence”. However, when I then manually rename the 2nd
column from 'PeptideModifiedSequence' to 'PeptideSequence', it does work. Is
this intended?

5) Finally, I have the
data from the regular proteomics experiment they did and was hoping to
integrate this into the PTM analysis (indeed, this is why I was so keen to try
MSstatsPTM in the first place, the paper convinced me it was worth it to invest the effort).
However, for this experiment the measurement was in DIA mode and the output I
got was from Spectronaut. Since the ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat function
expects the global_protein_input to also be in Progenesis format, is there a way
I can still integrate these two datasets? Perhaps by using the MSstats SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat
output and adding this to the ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat output somehow?

That was a lot, but if
any of you can give me some advice or pointers to help me get the analysis
correct, it would be greatly appreciated!

Please find in attach
some example screenshots to help illustrate these questions.

Kind regards,

Robin Colpaert

messages.body_plain:
Hello MSstats team,

I am analyzing a data set consisting of 2 groups, 3 replicates each. First, I am imputing the missing values and then performing groups comparison.
I noticed that in some cases the p-value is missing from the group comparison lines, specifically, when the ratio between the replicates that the protein was found in is 1:3 or 1:2 (In other words, when in group A the protein was found in 1 replicate from 3, and in group B in 2 replicates from 3). I am not sure if it has something to do with the imputation limit because the log2FC is present, but maybe im wrong.
If not, is there something wrong with my code or how can I overcome this problem?
I am attaching the r code I am using, and part of the output (The missing p-value lines I am talking about are 16, 17, 45, 48, 68, 84, 89, 94.)

Thank you in advance for all your help!

  raw,
  logTrans = 2,
  normalization = FALSE,
  normalization.PTM = FALSE,
  nameStandards = NULL,
  nameStandards.PTM = NULL,
  featureSubset = "all",
  featureSubset.PTM = "all",
  remove_uninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE,

  n_top_feature = "all",

  fix_missing = NULL,
  use_log_file = TRUE,
  append = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  log_file_path = NULL,
  base = "MSstatsPTM_log_"
  )

comarison_results <- groupComparisonPTM(
  analyzed_data,

  log_base = 2,
  use_log_file = TRUE,
  append = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  log_file_path = NULL,

)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Robin,

Apologies for the delayed response. I will address your points in order below. I do want to say off that the Progenesis converter is an older converter and it is possible that there are issues we will need to address.

1) I am assuming this second column is for peptides that were not uniquely identified as belonging to one protein. In this case the other protein is listed in the second column. These rows can be kept or removed based on if you want to use these non-unique ids.

2) You can safely filter out rows without a PTM. In terms of multiple PTMs, MSstatsPTM should keep these, but summarize these separately from single modified peptides.

3) These should be filtered out.

4) I think this is due to Progenesis is an old converter and you are totally fine updating the columns in this way.

5) This is possible, but will require a bit of manual work. What you need to do is run the proteome data separately with the MSstats converter, and then add it into the MSstatsPTM workflow. I have included a quick script to do this below.

```
library(MSstatsPTM)
library(MSstats)

MSstatsPTM_input = ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat(ptm_data, annotation_file)

MSstats_input = SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(protein_data, protein_annotation_file)

MSstatsPTM_input$PROTEIN = MSstats_input

summarized_data = dataSummarizationPTM(MSstatsPTM_input)
```

I hope this makes sense. Feel free to follow up with any additional questions/clarifications.

Devon

Also, if an experiment has an unbalanced design (2 groups; 5 BioReps and 4 BioReps), would we have to insert 4 for "NumSample" to determine the the other factors?

Thank you,

Frank

> Apologies for the delayed response. I will address your points in order below. I do want to say off that the Progenesis converter is an older converter and it is possible that there are issues we will need to address.
>
> 1) I am assuming this second column is for peptides that were not uniquely identified as belonging to one protein. In this case the other protein is listed in the second column. These rows can be kept or removed based on if you want to use these non-unique ids.
>
> 2) You can safely filter out rows without a PTM. In terms of multiple PTMs, MSstatsPTM should keep these, but summarize these separately from single modified peptides.
>
> 3) These should be filtered out.
>
> 4) I think this is due to Progenesis is an old converter and you are totally fine updating the columns in this way.
>
> 5) This is possible, but will require a bit of manual work. What you need to do is run the proteome data separately with the MSstats converter, and then add it into the MSstatsPTM workflow. I have included a quick script to do this below.
>
> ```
> library(MSstatsPTM)
> library(MSstats)
>
> MSstatsPTM_input = ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat(ptm_data, annotation_file)
>
> MSstats_input = SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(protein_data, protein_annotation_file)
>
> MSstatsPTM_input$PROTEIN = MSstats_input
>
> summarized_data = dataSummarizationPTM(MSstatsPTM_input)
> ```
>
> I hope this makes sense. Feel free to follow up with any additional questions/clarifications.
>
> Devon
